title: Backend work exponent envelope
statement: Let $\omega\in\mathbb Q$ be positive with $2\le\omega$, and let a linear solver backend have an exponent certificate: for each dimension coefficient $d$, row coefficient $r$, and degree $k$, it supplies a coefficient $c(d,r,k)$ such that, whenever $B>0$, the number of variables is at most $dB^k$, and the number of equations is at most $rB^k$, the backend work is at most $c(d,r,k)B^{\lceil\omega k\rceil}$. For nonnegative integers $n,\ell$, a parameter $0<\delta\le 1/2$, and any labeled sample sequence of the scheduled sample count, the learner's work is at most $C(\ell,\delta)(n+1)^{\lceil\omega\ell\rceil}$, where $C(\ell,\delta)=r(d+1)+c(d,r,\ell)$, $d=\ell+1$, and $r=2^\ell(\ell+b(\delta)+1)$ with $b(\delta)=\lceil\log_2\lceil2/\delta\rceil\rceil$.
hypotheses_covered: $\omega$ is a positive rational exponent and $2\le\omega$
the backend has a certificate giving the stated work bound for all finite equation systems and positive integer bases
the sample sequence has length equal to the scheduled sample count
